title: Pope Leo XIV Condemns AI Art as Slop in First AI Critique
summary:
The capacity of machines to synthesize millions of existing works does not grant them the ability to replicate the human spark behind art, the Vatican stated. Pope Leo XIV characterized machine-generated imagery as 'slop' and called for a clear distinction between AI content and work created by people, asserting that the two are fundamentally different in nature rather than just aesthetics.

The Catholic Church plans to strengthen alliances with artists and cultural institutions to protect uniquely human creativity. This intervention marks the Pope's first entry into the global debate regarding the legitimacy and distinction of AI-generated art.

Pope Leo XIV says machine-generated images are fundamentally different from human art, not just aesthetically, but in their very nature.

According to the Holy Father:

“Algorithms lack the spark of humanity.”

Now the Church wants to strengthen its alliance with artists and cultural institutions to protect what it sees as uniquely human creativity.
